name: Gleek
description: Gleek is a historical English three-player vying and trick-taking game played with a 44-card deck, combining stock bidding, ruff betting, declaration of sets, and 12-trick play.

overview.description: Gleek is a historical English three-player vying and trick-taking game played with a 44-card deck, combining stock bidding, ruff betting, declaration of sets, and 12-trick play.

history.origins: Gleek appears in English sources from the 16th century and was a major three-player game in the 16th-17th centuries.
timeline: 16th century: Early English references establish Gleek as a known play form.
17th century: Period descriptions from Cotgrave, Willughby, and Cotton record active play.
Modern era: Reconstructed by historical game researchers from surviving texts.
history.cultural: Gleek was a fashionable money game in early modern England and is frequently discussed in historical card-game scholarship.
history.evolution: Rules differ across historical reconstructions, especially in stock exchange procedure and some trick-stage interpretations.

setup.players: 3 players clockwise; eldest is left of dealer.
setup.deck: 44 cards ranked A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 in each suit (2s and 3s removed).
setup.dealing: Deal 12 cards to each player; place remaining 8 as stock and turn top card to set trump.
setup.equipment: Counters or stakes for pot payments.

rules.objective: Profit across phases by winning stock bid value lines, ruff vie pot, set declarations, and trick-stage point settlement.
rules.gameplay: A hand proceeds in four main stages: (1) bid for right to use stock; highest bidder pays bid amount split to opponents and exchanges by discarding and taking stock cards; (2) vie for Ruff, the highest valued suit total in hand (aces 11, courts 10, numerals face value), with betting actions similar to poker; (3) declare Mournivals (four of a kind) and Gleeks (three of a kind) for fixed payments from opponents; (4) play 12 tricks, eldest leading first trick, following suit when possible, with trump from turn-up card. Trick stage adds point settlement around trick count and honour values. Historical sources disagree on some details, so rule variants must be table-agreed before play.
keyRules: A gleek is three of a kind and a mournival is four of a kind.
Ruff compares best suit-point total, not generic hand rank.
Trick phase is fixed at 12 tricks with follow-suit requirement.
Extant reconstructions differ on specific edge rules; session must declare which reconstruction is authoritative.

strategy.basic: Preserve coherent suit concentration for Ruff while avoiding overpaying in stock bid stage.
strategy.intermediate: Estimate whether stock exchange can materially improve ruff or declaration equity before committing bid money.
strategy.advanced: Coordinate ruff-vie pressure with likely declaration payouts and expected trick-stage honour conversion.
tips: Do not treat stock and ruff stages independently; both consume stake and shape later trick value.
Before play, lock the table's interpretation of disputed historical details to avoid settlement disputes.

variations.name: Discard-Then-Take vs Take-Then-Discard
variations.description: Reconstructions differ on whether stock winner discards before taking stock or vice versa.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Stock exchange sequence is procedural; no engine constant overrides documented for this variant.

variations.name: Early Pass Interpretation
variations.description: Some tables treat initial pass in ruff vie as fold, others as check-like option before first vie.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Pass semantics are policy-only; add overrides when encoding specific reconstruction.

variations.name: Trump Side Payment Rules
variations.description: Optional side claims for trump Four (Tiddy) and optionally trump Five/Six are table-dependent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Side payment amounts vary by table; add overrides when implementing specific values.

scoring.description: Scoring combines phase-specific money transfers: stock bid payout, ruff pot, declaration payments, and trick-stage differential settlement.
scoring.winCondition: Session winner is player with greatest net stake profit over agreed number of hands.

synthesis.shortDescription: Complex three-player historical money game that chains bidding, suit-value vying, set declarations, and trick-point settlement.
